reason: As the child meets it, this item is no harder than the T3 calibration, and arguably easier. The carrier 'The lid was TRANSPARENT, so she could see the cake inside.' all but defines the word: 'so she could see ... inside' points straight at the key. The key 'clear' is a tier-1 word, and 'transparent' itself is taught by name in KS2 science on materials and light. Against that context the distractors fall away. 'thin' is one property, 'shiny' shares only the setting, and 'obvious' (the other meaning) is plainly wrong once the lid and the cake fix the see-through sense. The T3 items are bare cards with no context at all (hostile/unfriendly, vague/unclear, feeble/frail, genuine/real, reluctant/unwilling), so a carrier on a T3 headword is not harder than they are. The vr04 band '(T4-T5)' describes where carrier rows were authored. It is not a constraint on where an OM item may sit. checkVr04Row enforces only CARRIER vs BARE ('OM needs a carrier sentence') and has no tier test. The scarcity note's 'only headwords with two live senses AND a T4/T5 slot' explains why there are four OM rows, because that is where carrier slots were laid out; it does not forbid one elsewhere. Even the gate's own message, that a bare OM is wrong 'at T1-T3', is descriptive: bare cards sit at T4 and T5 too (bank-25 to bank-40). The protection the text exists for, that OM is a second correct answer without a carrier, is fully met here because this item has a carrier. Moving it leaves the OM row count at four. It also spreads OM across T3, T4 and T5 rather than removing it from T5, where exquisite still sits. That every other carrier item is T4 or T5 follows from their headwords' vault tiers (jubilant, conceal, exhausted, abundant, stoic at 4; notorious, exquisite, benevolent, jovial, luminous, melancholy at 5) under the same vocabTierOfSet derivation. It is not a format rule, so transparent at T3 is the same rule applied to a T3 headword. The one real cost is that this becomes the first carrier-format item a T3 child meets. That is a change of prompt wording ('Read the sentence...'), not of difficulty, and the carrier helps rather than hinders. Holding at T5 would leave a ratified vault move (David, 2026-08-02) and the derivation both saying 3 while the store serves 5, a disagreement nothing reports. A child at T5 would meet one of the easiest items in the type, and a T3 child would never meet it. The signature covers {stem, options, explanation}, not the tier, so the re-tier voids nothing. Standing note, not a ground here: my round-1 view stands that transparent's sense B (an excuse that fools nobody) is a figurative stretch children of this age rarely meet. That weakens 'obvious' as an OM trap without making it correct, and the carrier fixes the sense either way.
bankItemNote: Yes, bank-vr-04-closest-meaning-35 (bare transparent, clear/opaque/glass/window) should move to T3 by the same vault ruling. A bare card on a T3 headword with a tier-1 key sits with hostile, vague and genuine at T3, and as a bare card it has no OM distractor, so nothing about it needs T5. It needs its own review and is not changed here.
